brief: JPM's Tyler returns to a Tactically Bullish equity stance, reversing the Cautious/Neutral call made Aug 31 on Fed uncertainty, positioning, credit spreads, negative seasonality and the Momentum unwind; since that call SPX gained 75bp and the +NDX/-RTY pair returned 7.9%. The reversal rests on bond yields finding a level and oil trending lower (albeit choppily), which in turn rests on: Flash PMIs showing growth near 5% real GDP, implying SPX earnings estimates (29% for 26Q3 after 52% in 26Q2) are too low because EPS growth tracks nominal not real GDP; consumer spending defying expectations, refuting the K-shaped read; and Barry's forecast that the 10Y eases to 5.05% by year-end, reducing bond vol. JPM still likes Tech as a core long but drops the -RTY short hedge on squeeze risk if a US/Iran deal lowers oil and yields, preferring a derivative expression instead; ex-Tech it favors Banks over rate-sensitive sectors. Three deal/no-deal scenarios from last week still frame the risk.
